733050101.text: ...Be careful. I feel some strange tremors from deep underground.

733050103.text: It's nothing... That was just a drill.

733050104.text: Oh... So it was just a drill!

733050105.text: Wait... What kind of drill are you talking about!?

733051203.text: It's nothing... That was just a drill.

733051204.text: Oh... So it was just a drill!

733051205.text: Wait... What kind of drill are you talking about!?

733052201.text: Please connect me with that chess piece.

733052203.text: Find the protrusion on its surface and insert that into the slot on my bottle. It's as simple as that.

733052204.text: Huh... there's a slot on your bottle? But it looks pretty smooth... There's no place to plug it in!

733052205.text: It's there. You just can't see it...

733052209.text: Ha... Alright, that's enough jokes for now. All you have to do, my master, is to hold me and touch the chess piece.

733050402.text: Hmm... Liloupar, are you alright? Why are you so quiet?

733050405.text: Wait... Look. She's glowing. Well, differently from normal, anyway...

733050406.text: The Jinni's bottle shimmers, seemingly in tune with the vibration of the chess piece.\nYou can hear the passing of time like drops of water in a prison... It seems to last a lifetime, or perhaps just for a moment.\nLiloupar doesn't say a word.

733050407.text: Then, out of the mist, you see a great city, big, bloated, and cold.\nThe earth opens up, swallowing everything in Gurabad...\nAnd there stands its gate, set in the mountain wall. It is loathsome, seeming almost to contain all the filth of the ancient world that somehow escaped the people's gaze...

733050408.text: That's Gurabad over there. I remember it now.

733050410.text: Whoa, what's the matter with you guys... Can't you let Paimon know in advance next time? These surprises are bad for Paimon's heart!

733050501.text: Whoa! We were just next to that chess piece. Then things went "whoosh," and now we're here!

733050502.text: How did this happen? That's really awesome!

733050503.text: Hehe, and would you like a repeat performance?

733050505.text: Hey, show some restraint! What are you, a kid?

733050508.text: That is normal. The coordinates are somewhat off. Perhaps the device is showing its age...

733050509.text: Hey... Isn't this the valley we first went to? What are you bringing us here for? Is there anything worth seeing here?

733050510.text: You ask too many questions, little one.

733050511.text: Strange... It was supposed to be here... Ah, here it is!

733050507.text: Now that you mention it... Paimon's head feels a little woozy, too...

733050601.text: Whoa! We were just next to that chess piece. Then things went "whoosh," and now we're here!

733050603.text: Hehe, and would you like a repeat performance?

733050610.text: You ask too many questions, little one.

733050611.text: Strange... It was supposed to be here... Ah, here it is!

733050607.text: Now that you mention it... Paimon's head feels a little woozy, too...

733050702.text: Behold Gurabad. Once, it was swallowed by the very earth itself — now, it lies before you.

733050703.text: Ah. It would seem that this place has some new tenants. Please do get rid of them, my master.

733050801.text: "Shiruyeh is Khorramdin." \nThus says the man in the brass mask.

733050802.text: "There will be no heirs to your name. I will do away with the many idols in your temples. I will consign you to your grave, for such does one as despicable as you deserve."\nSays the man in the brass mask.

733050803.text: Through the Jinni's entranced eyes, you bear witness to Gurabad as it is engulfed in darkness... \nThe city of Gurabad has long been a reservoir of water, but now its inhabitants scatter like a torrent. \nThe Jinn, devoid of intellect, pour out from cold machine husks, from the soldiers' weapons... And the scarlet wine, the juice of the pomegranate, bursts forth...

733050804.text: The pomegranates are crushed and cracked, and they are trampled into a mass of mud... Plump or withered, rich or humble... The scarlet fruits, with hue and cry, tell of the Khorramdin's coming — the joy of life and the joy of vengeance.\nThe juice tastes as sweet and mellow as sweet wine, and flows through the city, turning the reservoir into a vast red sea... \nThe sea first drowns the slaves, and then their masters howl as they flounder amidst the roiling waves of night.

733050805.text: Finally, you see the brass-masked king. He flees into the shadows — into Shirin's arms... \nHer face is old and dim, all traces of life and reason having vanished from it like dust in the night's wind.\nAnd then there is King Kisra, who turned into a dark monster... they all are your flesh and blood, yet you rejoice, and you exult in that retribution.

733050806.text: O Gurabad, you are mortally stricken, your shame shown to all...\nAll who receive these tidings shall clap and shout for joy...\nFor is there anyone who has not felt your unending tyranny?

733050807.text:
You hold the magic bottle to your ear...
There is a chuckle, and you hear someone whispering in your ear in a gentle and delicate language...
She speaks of things as unknowable as a deep spring, but you comprehend it all.
And at last, the words dissipate, leaving only a cool tingling in your ear...

733050808.text: Through her guidance, you have become familiar with the ancient verses... \nBut she speaks no more.

733050901.text: As the shard of light merges with Liloupar's magic bottle, you feel a little of your own power being pulled away...

733050908.text: "O Gurabad, you are mortally stricken, your shame shown to all..."

733050911.text: Ormazd was once the lover of the one called Liloupar. It was by the Jinni's love that he rose from a lowly shepherd to become a king amongst mortals.

733050912.text: I once believed that he was no mere mortal companion. Foolishly, I fell for those eyes of his... But the vanity and selfishness that kings are wont to have seized him in the end.

733050913.text: He turned out to be no different from those mortal rulers who live one day and die the next, wandering amidst dreams of conquest and persecution, building their palaces upon quicksand.

733050915.text: Like I said, I punished him — handed ruin down from father to son, across three generations.

733050916.text: Kisra Parvezravan, Shirin, they are my blood... It was by schemes of blood, honeyed execution, and raging ambition that I punished them all.

733050917.text: But that was not all... *sigh* That was not all.
